q: The equipotential surfaces around a point charge $Q$ are _____ surfaces centred about the charge $Q$.
e: A point charge is small enough that its own size can be ignored next to the other distances. The equipotential surfaces around a point charge Q are spherical surfaces centred about the charge Q. Cylindrical or planar is not this quantity.

q: The electric lines of force are _____ to the equipotential surfaces.
e: The electric lines of force are perpendicular to the equipotential surfaces. Do not trade perpendicular for parallel or tangent.

q: The surface of a charged conducting sphere is an equipotential surface because the charges distributed uniformly on its surface are _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The surface of a charged conducting sphere is an equipotential surface because the charges distributed uniformly on its surface are stationary. Do not trade stationary for moving or oscillating.

q: If the surface of a conductor is not an equipotential surface, there will be a potential difference and the charges would _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. If the surface of a conductor is not an equipotential surface, there will be a potential difference and the charges would move. Do not trade move for stop or vanish.

q: The work done is _____ in bringing a charge from one point to another point on an equipotential surface.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work done is zero in bringing a charge from one point to another point on an equipotential surface. Maximum or minimum is not this quantity.

q: Charged conductors may have any shape but their surfaces are all _____ surfaces.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Charged conductors may have any shape but their surfaces are all equipotential surfaces. Do not trade equipotential for magnetic or gravitational.

q: The electric lines of force are perpendicular to the _____ of the charged conductor.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The electric lines of force are perpendicular to the surface of the charged conductor. Volume or centre is not this quantity.

q: The equipotential surfaces around a charge $Q$ are spherical surfaces _____ about the charge $Q$.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The equipotential surfaces around a charge Q are spherical surfaces centred about the charge Q. Offset or tangent is not this quantity.

q: Moving a charge along an equipotential surface requires _____ work.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Moving a charge along an equipotential surface requires zero work. Do not trade zero for maximum or negative.

q: If the surface of a charged conductor is not an equipotential surface, there will be a _____ difference.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. If the surface of a charged conductor is not an equipotential surface, there will be a potential difference. Do not trade potential for temperature or pressure.
